content.title: About
content.content: Fruit smoothie is made from whole fruits without any dairy ingredients. It contains added plant protein, making the drink nutritious and suitable for vegans and those monitoring protein intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blends can include banana, berries, mango, pineapple and other seasonal fruits.
The absence of dairy makes the smoothie suitable for people with lactose intolerance.
Added plant protein is often derived from pea, hemp or soy.
Fruit smoothie retains most vitamins and minerals thanks to the use of whole fruits.
The recipe can be tweaked for specific goals, such as adding chia seeds, flax or nut milk.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and antioxidants
items.content: Fruits provide vitamin C, vitamin A, folate and polyphenols that support immunity and protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports muscle growth
items.content: The added plant protein supplies about 15–20 g of protein per serving, aiding muscle recovery after workouts.

items.title: Improves digestion
items.content: Fiber from whole fruits promotes regular bowel movements and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low sugar when using appropriate fruits
items.content: Choosing berries and low‑sugar fruits helps keep the glycemic index of the drink moderate.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content of fruits helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Allergy to plant protein
items.content: Some individuals may react to pea, soy or hemp protein.

items.title: High natural fruit sugars
items.content: Large amounts of sweet fruits can make the smoothie calorie‑dense and raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Digestive issues from excess fiber
items.content: Very large servings may cause bloating or diarrhea in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the smoothie immediately after blending to preserve vitamins. It works well as a breakfast, post‑workout snack, or light dinner. Optionally garnish with chia seeds, nuts or fresh berries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the blend in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Longer storage may lead to flavor loss and reduced vitamin levels.

content.title: About
content.content: Hot Pepper Sauce is a concentrated condiment made from fresh or dried hot peppers, vinegar, salt, and sometimes additional spices. It delivers a bright, fiery flavor and high heat, perfect for adding a punch to a variety of dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Capsaicin content is responsible for the burning sensation and has a thermogenic effect.
Traditionally prepared in Southeast Asian, Mexican, and Caribbean cuisines.
Variants range from mild to extreme, some exceeding 100,000 Scoville units.
Vinegar stabilizes the flavor and extends shelf life.
Often used as a base for marinades, dressings, and cocktails.

items.title: Rich in capsaicin
items.content: Capsaicin may boost metabolism, aid calorie burning, and improve circulation.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Peppers provide vitamin C and carotenoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Spicy foods stimulate gastric juice production, enhancing digestion.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The sauce contains modest amounts of B‑vitamins, potassium, and iron.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Capsaicin triggers endorphin release, which can improve mood.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Consuming large amounts may cause heartburn or irritation of the stomach lining.

items.title: Pepper allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper components.

items.title: Increased body temperature
items.content: Capsaicin can cause temporary rise in body temperature and sweating.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Spicy sauces may enhance the effects of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for those on such medication.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the sauce in small amounts to soups, stews, meat dishes, pizza, tacos, salads, or use it as a marinade. It can be blended with mayo or sour cream for a milder dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator. Properly stored, it retains flavor and heat for up to 6 months. Discard if mold, discoloration, or off‑odors develop.

oatmeal-instant-plain-made-with-milk-fat.title: Oatmeal, instant, plain, made with milk, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Instant oatmeal is a quick‑soluble product made from whole oat grains that have been steamed and dried into fine flakes. This version is prepared with milk and has added fat (vegetable or dairy), giving it a richer, creamier taste and higher energy content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown for over 5,000 years.
Instant oatmeal was developed in the 1960s for convenient fast meals.
Adding fat can increase vitamin D levels when dairy fat is used.
Oats contain beta‑glucans, soluble fibers that help lower cholesterol.
Instant oatmeal can be customized with dried fruit, nuts, or spices.

items.title: Rich in beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans help regulate blood sugar and reduce cholesterol.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides sustained energy and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin B1 and magnesium
items.content: Vitamin B1 supports the nervous system, magnesium aids muscle function.

items.title: Added fat increases caloric density
items.content: The fat makes the product more energy‑dense, useful for higher calorie needs.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Thermal processing softens oats, making them gentle on the digestive tract.

items.title: Oat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to oats or added ingredients.

items.title: High calorie content from fat
items.content: Overconsumption can contribute to weight gain.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment that handles wheat, so trace gluten may be present.

items.title: Added sugars in flavored versions
items.content: If sweeteners or flavorings are added, sugar content rises.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 200 ml hot milk over the oatmeal, stir, and let stand for 1–2 minutes. Add fresh berries, nuts, honey, or cinnamon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a sealed package. For storage longer than 6 months, keep in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.

content.title: About
content.content: Pork steak coated with breadcrumbs is a cut of pork that has been breaded with a mixture of crumbs, spices and sometimes egg, then fried. The coating creates a crunchy exterior while the interior stays juicy and tender.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The coating often contains a blend of breadcrumbs, herbs and spices, giving the dish a fragrant flavor.
Breaded pork steak is popular in fast‑food and home cooking, especially when served with barbecue or mustard sauces.
Traditionally the crumbs are made from white bread, but whole‑grain or gluten‑free alternatives can be used.
When fried correctly, the crust remains crisp even after a short rest in sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies thiamine, niacin, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of zinc and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation and oxygen transport.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Lean portions of pork contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that can support heart health when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein and moderate fat content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Processing and additives
items.content: Breaded products may contain salt, trans‑fats and preservatives; people with high blood pressure or sensitivities should choose additive‑free versions.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: A coated steak is more calorie‑dense than a lean, unbreaded cut.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The crunchy crust can encourage rapid eating, leading to excess intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional breadcrumbs contain wheat; those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity need a gluten‑free coating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: For best results, pan‑fry the coated steak over medium heat until golden, then finish in a 180 °C oven for 10‑15 minutes. Serve with roasted vegetables, mashed potatoes or a fresh salad. Complement with sauces such as barbecue, mustard or creamy dill.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked steak in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag at –18 °C, where it remains good for 2‑3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate waffle is a delicate dessert made from a batter enriched with cocoa powder and topped with a glossy chocolate glaze. It features a crisp outer crust and a soft, slightly airy interior, combining the sweetness of chocolate with the lightness of the waffle.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Waffles originated in medieval Europe, and chocolate versions became popular in the early 20th century.
Traditional waffles are baked in patterned iron presses that give them their characteristic grid.
Chocolate waffles are often served with berries, ice cream, or whipped cream.
Cocoa powder adds aroma, dark color, and antioxidants to the batter.
Waffles can be sweet or mildly bitter depending on the type of chocolate used.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa contains flavonoids that help combat free radicals and support heart health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Chocolate waffles provide a quick source of energy through carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat.

items.title: Magnesium content
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The batter supplies vitamins B1, B2, and B3, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, helping to lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The batter typically contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine and theobromine, which may cause jitteriness in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate waffles are fairly calorie‑dense, so they should be enjoyed in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the waffle warm, straight from the iron or slightly cooled. It is commonly served with fresh berries, fruit sauce, ice cream, whipped cream, or an extra drizzle of chocolate glaze.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store waffles in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze them, first wrapping tightly in plastic film.
